title: 14 vvhat frevvyll remayneth in man after ſynne.

segments.text:
NOtwithſtanding we denye not a but that men haue ſufficiente light to make them without ex
••ſe. And to ſpoile them not, nor dipriue 〈…〉em of their naturall faculties and po
•ers, as of reaſon, Iudgement, wyll ſuche others to make them ſtockes or •okes, nor yet of frewyll: ſo that they •igne this to it, that al is nothing but darknes and enemitie againſt god, and
that by this worde frewyl be not vnderſtand a naturall power to thinke, wy• or doe good or euell, but a wyll not conſtrayned the whiche not withſtanding cannot nor wyll not any thyng but altogether euyll, ſo much is the nature •• mā not being regenerate (that is to ſa• not healed nor reſtored by grace (not onlye wounded or hurt, but vtterly and altogether corrupted and alſo willyngly becom y• ſeruant of ſinne. Therfore ſaid S. Auguſtine, that the faulte whych• folowed the ſynne and whiche is the puniſhement hathe tourned lybertye into neceſſitie. Item frewyl as it is bound and thralle is nothinge worthe but to ſynne and fall.
